description: Google Calendar OAuth integration: DB migration, encryption helpers, OAuth routes, calendar helper library, 1-on-1 Calendar wiring (create/update/delete events + google_event_id column), and IntegrationsClient UI update.
steps: 1. Create supabase/migrations/20261023000019_google_calendar_connections.sql. Table: google_calendar_connections(id uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE UNIQUE, access_token_ciphertext text NOT NULL, refresh_token_ciphertext text NOT NULL, token_expiry timestamptz, calendar_id text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'primary', created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()). Enable RLS. Add policy 'users_own_google_calendar_connections' FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (user_id = auth.uid()) WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid()). Add policy 'anon_no_access_google_calendar_connections' FOR ALL TO anon USING (false). GRANT ALL ON google_calendar_connections TO service_role. Add set_updated_at trigger (same pattern as slack_connections migration).
2. Create supabase/migrations/20261023000020_one_on_ones_google_event_id.sql. Add column: ALTER TABLE one_on_ones ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS google_event_id text;

3. Add GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=, GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=, GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY= placeholder lines to .env.local (after the existing GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET= line that already partially exists). Check first — GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET already exist as blank; only add GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI and GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY if missing.

4. Create src/lib/google-calendar.ts. Export: (a) getGoogleConfig() — reads GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI env vars, throws if missing. (b) encryptGoogleToken(value: string): string — AES-256-GCM using GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var (base64, 32 bytes), same 'v1:iv:tag:ciphertext' format as encryptAsanaToken in src/lib/asana.ts. (c) decryptGoogleToken(value: string): string — matching decrypt. (d) getGoogleAccessToken(userId: string): Promise<string> — queries google_calendar_connections for user, decrypts access_token_ciphertext; if token_expiry is within 60 seconds of now, POSTs to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token with grant_type=refresh_token using decrypted refresh_token, updates the DB row with new encrypted tokens and expiry, returns new access token. (e) createCalendarEvent(userId: string, opts: { title: string; description?: string; startAt: string; endAt: string; attendeeEmails: string[] }): Promise<{ eventId: string; htmlLink: string }> — calls Google Calendar REST API POST https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{calendarId}/events, reads calendarId from the DB row (default 'primary'), returns eventId and htmlLink. (f) updateCalendarEvent(userId: string, eventId: string, opts: { title?: string; description?: string; startAt?: string; endAt?: string }): Promise<void> — PATCH to same endpoint. (g) deleteCalendarEvent(userId: string, eventId: string): Promise<void> — DELETE to same endpoint. All functions use supabaseAdmin from src/lib/supabase. All calendar calls are non-throwing on missing connection (return null / no-op gracefully when user has no row).

5. Create src/app/api/integrations/google-calendar/connect/route.ts. Pattern: identical to asana connect route. State cookie name 'kazi_gcal_oauth'. Build Google OAuth URL: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with params client_id, redirect_uri (GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI), response_type=code, scope='https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events openid email', access_type=offline, prompt=consent, state. Read session with getServerSession(authOptions), redirect to /login if missing. Redirect to Google OAuth URL.

6. Create src/app/api/integrations/google-calendar/callback/route.ts. Pattern: mirrors asana callback. Cookie name 'kazi_gcal_oauth'. Exchange code: POST to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token with code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code. Response gives access_token, refresh_token, expires_in. Fetch user email from https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo with the access_token (for logging; not stored separately). Upsert into google_calendar_connections: { user_id, access_token_ciphertext: encryptGoogleToken(access_token), refresh_token_ciphertext: encryptGoogleToken(refresh_token), token_expiry: new Date(Date.now() + expires_in*1000).toISOString(), calendar_id: 'primary' } with onConflict: 'user_id'. On success redirect to /settings/integrations?google_calendar=connected. On any error redirect to /settings/integrations?google_calendar=error.

7. Create src/app/api/integrations/google-calendar/disconnect/route.ts. DELETE method, getServerSession auth guard, delete from google_calendar_connections where user_id = session.user.id, return { ok: true }.

8. Create src/app/api/integrations/google-calendar/status/route.ts. GET method, getServerSession auth guard, query google_calendar_connections for user, return { connected: boolean, calendar_id: string | null }.

9. Update src/app/api/pulse/one-on-ones/route.ts (POST). After the successful insert + invalidateOneOnOneParticipants call: (a) fetch manager and report user names from supabaseAdmin .from('users').select('id,name,email').in('id', [managerId, reportId]); (b) if scheduledAt is set, attempt createCalendarEvent — import from src/lib/google-calendar.ts. Wrap in try/catch (non-blocking). If successful, UPDATE the one_on_ones row to set google_event_id = result.eventId. The insert returns id; use that to update. Attendee emails come from the fetched users. Title: '1-on-1: {managerName} & {reportName}'. Description: 'Scheduled via Kazi'. startAt = scheduledAt, endAt = new Date(new Date(scheduledAt).getTime() + 60*60*1000).toISOString() (default 1 hour). POST already returns { id, carried }; keep that unchanged.

10. Update src/app/api/pulse/one-on-ones/[id]/route.ts (PATCH). (a) Accept scheduledAt in the request body alongside agenda, notes, action_items. Add it to the update object if present. (b) After the successful DB update: if scheduledAt is in the request and existing row has google_event_id, call updateCalendarEvent with new scheduledAt (non-blocking try/catch). If scheduledAt is set but there's no google_event_id yet, call createCalendarEvent and then UPDATE the row with the returned eventId (also non-blocking). Fetch manager/report user names for attendees using existing row's manager_id/report_id. (c) Add DELETE handler to same file: GET the existing row (select manager_id, report_id, google_event_id), call deleteCalendarEvent if google_event_id is set (non-blocking), then delete the row from one_on_ones. Return { ok: true }.

11. Update src/types/database.ts. (a) Add google_calendar_connections table to the Database interface Tables section (after asana_connections): Row { id: string; user_id: string; access_token_ciphertext: string; refresh_token_ciphertext: string; token_expiry: string | null; calendar_id: string; created_at: string; updated_at: string }. Insert: Omit<Row, 'id'|'created_at'|'updated_at'|'token_expiry'|'calendar_id'> & { token_expiry?: string|null; calendar_id?: string }. Update: Partial<Row>. (b) Add google_event_id: string | null to one_on_ones Row, and add it as optional (google_event_id?: string|null) to Insert and Update. (c) Add type alias: export type GoogleCalendarConnection = Database['public']['Tables']['google_calendar_connections']['Row'];

12. Update src/app/(app)/settings/integrations/page.tsx. Add query for google_calendar_connections: const { data: gcalRow } = await supabaseAdmin.from('google_calendar_connections').select('calendar_id, created_at').eq('user_id', session.user.id).maybeSingle(). Pass googleCalendarStatus={{ connected: Boolean(gcalRow), calendarId: gcalRow?.calendar_id ?? null }} to IntegrationsClient.

13. Update src/features/settings/components/IntegrationsClient.tsx. (a) Add GoogleCalendarStatus interface { connected: boolean; calendarId: string | null }. Add it to Props. (b) Add googleCalendar state from prop. (c) Add useEffect branch for ?google_calendar=connected and ?google_calendar=error query params (same pattern as asana useEffect). (d) Add connectGoogleCalendar() that sets window.location.href = '/api/integrations/google-calendar/connect'. (e) Add disconnectGoogleCalendar() that DELETEs /api/integrations/google-calendar/disconnect. (f) Add a new 'Productivity' SettingsSection (icon 'solar:calendar-broken') with a single IntegrationCard for Google Calendar (icon 'logos:google-calendar', status based on googleCalendar.connected, meta: calendarId display if connected, onConnect/onDisconnect wired up). (g) Remove Google Calendar from the 'Coming soon' grid — it now appears in the Productivity section.
acceptance_criteria: Migration 20261023000019 creates google_calendar_connections with RLS: users can read/write only their own row, service_role has full access.
Migration 20261023000020 adds google_event_id text column to one_on_ones.
src/lib/google-calendar.ts exports getGoogleConfig, encryptGoogleToken, decryptGoogleToken, getGoogleAccessToken (with refresh logic), createCalendarEvent, updateCalendarEvent, deleteCalendarEvent.
GET /api/integrations/google-calendar/connect redirects to Google OAuth URL with correct scopes and state cookie.
GET /api/integrations/google-calendar/callback exchanges code, stores encrypted tokens, redirects to /settings/integrations?google_calendar=connected.
POST /api/pulse/one-on-ones creates a calendar event when scheduledAt is provided and manager has a google_calendar_connections row; stores eventId on the row.
PATCH /api/pulse/one-on-ones/[id] accepts scheduledAt and updates/creates calendar event accordingly.
DELETE /api/pulse/one-on-ones/[id] deletes the calendar event if google_event_id is set, then deletes the row.
src/types/database.ts includes google_calendar_connections table type and GoogleCalendarConnection alias; one_on_ones includes google_event_id.
IntegrationsClient shows a Productivity section with Google Calendar card (connect/disconnect, connected state); ?google_calendar=connected and ?google_calendar=error params are handled on load.
Google Calendar is removed from the Coming soon section.
verification: npx tsc --noEmit  (run from /Users/Apple/code/clients/kazi — must exit 0 with no errors)
npm run build  (must complete without type or build errors)
findings: google_calendar_connections table type uses a flat Insert shape (not Omit-self-reference) to avoid Supabase type inference returning 'never' — keep this pattern for any new tables added. google_event_id column added to one_on_ones Row/Insert/Update in database.ts. All calendar calls are non-blocking (try/catch, return null on missing connection). GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI and GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY placeholder lines added to .env.local (both blank — operator must fill before using the integration). The DatabaseTypes self-reference issue: avoid Omit<Database['public']['Tables'][tableName]['Row'], ...> inside Insert — use explicit field lists instead.
